content: From these results, we see that the logit trick clearly improves performance, which is consistent with the observations of Nogueira et al. BIBREF7. In fact, applying this technique in the zero-shot setting yields performance that is clearly better than random. Another interesting finding is that the choice of target token appears to have an impact on performance, which is also consistent with the above work. Since using true/false as the target token (conditions #3 and #4) did not improve performance much over conditions with entailment/contradiction, we did not run all data size conditions given our limited computational resources.
